cls: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (dual L-type and N-type)
quick: Usually taken after breakfast; may take with or without food
Avoid unless clearly needed; safety not established
Use with caution; usually no major adjustment (low renal excretion)
Use with caution / lower dose; hepatically metabolized
Blood pressure, heart rate, peripheral edema
summary: Cilnidipine (the intended drug for the entry 'Clinidipine') is a fourth-generation dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that uniquely blocks both L-type (vascular) and N-type (sympathetic nerve) calcium channels. It is used to treat essential hypertension, lowering blood pressure with less reflex tachycardia and a lower incidence of pedal edema than conventional dihydropyridines. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on EMA/SmPC, BNF and reference (Japanese/Indian product) information.
indications: Hypertension where reduction of sympathetic activity or proteinuria is desirable (supportive evidence)

dosage.n: Start at 5 mg; titrate to response

admin: Take once daily, usually after breakfast, at about the same time each day
Check blood pressure regularly and titrate the dose to response
Do not stop abruptly without medical advice
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially when starting
moa: Cilnidipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium through voltage-dependent L-type channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing arterial vasodilation and reduced peripheral resistance and blood pressure. Distinctively, it also blocks N-type calcium channels on sympathetic nerve terminals, suppressing norepinephrine release. This dual action lowers blood pressure while limiting reflex sympathetic activation (less tachycardia) and is associated with renoprotective effects and a lower incidence of dihydropyridine-induced pedal edema.
preg: Safety in pregnancy is not established; dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are used in pregnancy only when the benefit outweighs the risk. Avoid unless clearly needed and consider better-characterized alternatives.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; it is not well established whether cilnidipine is excreted in human milk. Avoid or discontinue breastfeeding.
renal: Cilnidipine has low renal excretion; major dose adjustment is generally not required, but use with caution in significant renal impairment and monitor blood pressure.
hepatic: Cilnidipine is metabolized by the liver (CYP3A4); in hepatic impairment exposure may increase. Start at a low dose and titrate carefully.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, macrolides, HIV protease inhibitors) - increase cilnidipine levels and hypotension risk
moderate: Other antihypertensives, diuretics, nitrates - additive blood-pressure lowering
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce cilnidipine effect
Beta-blockers - generally complementary but monitor for excessive hypotension
minor: Digoxin - monitor levels (class caution with calcium channel blockers)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; commonly given after breakfast. Avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition).
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it may enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect and cause dizziness.

emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling/breathing difficulty
Signs of liver injury (jaundice, dark urine)

monitoring: Liver function tests in hepatic impairment or on long-term therapy
counsel: Take once daily, usually after breakfast, at the same time each day
You may feel dizzy or flushed at first - get up slowly and avoid driving until you know how it affects you
Do not stop suddenly; keep taking it even if you feel well, as high blood pressure often has no symptoms
Report swelling of the ankles, severe dizziness/fainting, or yellowing of skin or eyes
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice and tell your doctor about all other medicines
pk: Blood-pressure lowering begins within hours of dosing
Peak plasma concentration about 2-3 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 5-9 hours; pharmacodynamic effect outlasts plasma levels
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: The entry 'Clinidipine' refers to CILNIDIPINE; NOT FDA-approved - this record is based on EMA/SmPC, BNF and reference (Japanese/Indian) product information
Dual L-type AND N-type calcium channel blocker - reduces sympathetic outflow, giving less reflex tachycardia
Lower incidence of pedal edema than older dihydropyridines such as amlodipine
Has demonstrated reduction of proteinuria/renoprotective effects in studies
Metabolized by CYP3A4 - watch for interactions with strong inhibitors/inducers and grapefruit
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not take two doses together.
overdose: Overdose may cause excessive peripheral vasodilation with marked and prolonged hypotension, reflex tachycardia and flushing. Treatment is supportive: place the patient supine with legs raised, give intravenous fluids, and use vasopressors and intravenous calcium as needed; monitor cardiac and respiratory function. Dialysis is unlikely to help given high protein binding.
